newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia rolls out first plane with U.S. parts.
newsitem.headline: Russia rolls out first plane with U.S. parts.

text.p: Russia unveiled its first plane powered by U.S. engines on Saturday, hoping the unprecedented cooperation will help it break into world aviation markets.

The $70 million wide-body Il-96T cargo plane, built by leading Russian plane manufacturing group Ilyushin with U.S.-made engines and avionics, rolled out of a hangar at a ceremony attended by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

The freighter, which can carry 50 tonnes over 11,000 km (6,875 miles) or 92 tonnes over 5,000 km (3,125 miles) was unveiled at the Voronezh aviation plant several months late due to a lack of financing.

The chief designer of the Ilyushin group, Genrikh Novozhilov, said the aircraft would begin test flights soon and Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines -- its sole customer so far -- would get the plane in September.
Aeroflot spokesman Alexander Luchaninov said that two other freighters would be delivered in 1998 as well as the first passenger version known as Il-96M.

Aeroflot ordered a total of 20 planes with delivery by 2001 in a deal worth $1.5 billion to be funded by the U.S. Eximbank and several European and Russian banks with financial guarantees from the Russian goverment.
U.S. Pratt and Whitney, a division of United Technologies Corporation, is participating in the project.

"We hope Il-96M/T will be certified in Russia and in the United States," Marshall Robinson, general manager of Russian airframe programmes at Pratt and Whitney, told Reuters, adding that it would have good potential to be marketed outside Russia.

Chernomyrdin, who flew to Voronezh, 550 km (340 miles) south of Moscow for the ceremony, said that international deals such as this one could provide a much-needed fillip to the country's struggling aviation industry.
"Cooperation with Western plane-makers may be the shortest way to get Russian aircraft on the international market," Chernomyrdin told reporters.

A senior official from the Ilyushin group, which is made up of a design bureau and two aviation plants, said the company needed 125 billion roubles ($22 million) to buy parts for the planes it planned to make for Aeroflot.
"We hope to get a loan from the National Reserve Bank and other financial structures," he said.

But Novozhilov said the commercial bank's demands were not good for his company. "We are not very pleased by these conditions. But if the state cannot finance the industry we have to work with private sector," he said.
